title: Canary Custodian Field Guide (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working field guide for the person(s) who will act as the Canary Custodian during progressive releases (canaries, micro-releases, and A/B runs). Goal: give a concise checklist and decision heuristics so a single human or small team can safely shepherd incremental exposure for latency-sensitive LLM features.

Quick intent:
- Make canary stewardship low-friction and repeatable.
- Prioritize early detection of behavioral drift, latency/cost regressions, and user-visible failures.
- Preserve fast rollback paths and clear comms.

Role definitions (short):
- Canary Custodian: owns the canary lifecycle for the activation window. Runs checklist, triggers roll/unroll, coordinates oncall.
- Steward Lead: product/pm who owns success criteria and stakeholder comms.
- Observer(s): SRE/telemetry, model owner, and solutions engineer.

Pre-launch (T-48h):
- Confirm hypothesis and acceptance criteria with Steward Lead (primary metric, guardrail metrics).
- Validate telemetry hooks exist: latency p50/p95, token-cost, error-rate, safety-rate, top-k hallucination probe.
- Synthetic smoke: run 1000 deterministic queries against canary slice, assert no catastrophic failures.
- Check routing: ensure fallback policy and model variant mapping present.
- Canary cohort list: export identifiers for microcohorts (hash range, country, platform).
- Slack channel created: #canary-<feature>-<date> and escalation roster pinned.

Activation (T0):
- Start at low exposure (0.5% or 1% depending on risk). Timer: 30m observation window.
- Confirm synthetic probe passes within 10m.
- Live telemetry baseline: compare canary vs control for the same cohort. Important signals: latency delta, token consumption delta, error-rate spike, safety flag rate, successful fallback rate.
- If any critical signal breach -> immediate pause + notify oncall + move to rollback checklist.

Scaling steps (example cadence):
- 0.5% -> 2% (1h) -> 5% (2h) -> 15% (4h) -> 50% (8h) -> 100% (manual)
- Each step: min observation 1h for user-visible metrics, otherwise 30m for low-risk experiments.

Decision heuristics (fast checks):
- Severity-first: 1) safety violation (auto-stop), 2) 3x baseline error-rate (auto-stop), 3) latency p95 > baseline + 300ms (consider freeze), 4) cost-per-request > +25% (steward review).
- Signal concordance: if 2+ non-safety signals deviate in same direction, escalate.

Canary-specific probes to implement (examples):
- Hallucination spike: run labeled eval set and measure F1/precision drift.
- Regression prompts: sample 200 recent production prompts and compare output similarity or rejection rate.
- Token delta probe: track mean tokens per response for cohort vs baseline.
- Rerank integrity: for rerank models, track pairwise order flips and quality drop.

Human-in-loop flow (when to intervene):
- Soft alerts: annotate in thread; Custodian monitors for next step.
- Hard alerts: push rollback immediately.
- If ambiguous: reduce exposure by half and extend observation for 2x.

Rollback checklist (fast):
- Step 1: Pause exposure in control plane (console shortcut).
- Step 2: Switch cohort to fallback model (idempotent mapping).
- Step 3: Post to #canary channel with template: summary + metrics snapshot + time + action.
- Step 4: File incident stub (JIRA) for postmortem and tag owner.
- Step 5: If rollback due to safety, preserve input examples and attach to incident briefing.

Comms templates (short):
- Initial activation: "Activating canary for <feature> at <time>. Exposure: 0.5%. Custodian: @<name>. Observing p50/p95, error-rate, safety. Channel: #canary-<feature>-<date>."
- Pause/rollback: "Paused canary at <time>. Trigger: <signal>. Rolling back to <model>. Follow-up: incident <id>."

Microcohort design notes:
- Prefer orthogonal slices (platform, country, new-users) over ad-hoc demographics. Keep cohorts stable during run.
- Use consistent hashing so cohort membership is deterministic across runs.
- For small power-sensitive features, prefer stratified sampling to ensure each cohort has enough events.

A/B power-aware guidance:
- Precompute minimum exposure to reach desired statistical power for the primary metric. If required exposure > 15%, talk to Steward Lead about budget and staging.
- When running paired A/B for quality differences: make sure matching traffic volumes are enforced per cohort.

Automation hooks to build (TODO):
- Auto-snapshot generator: collect top 20 diffing queries when drift detected.
- Canary annealer: automatically hold scale for N minutes if drift seen in previous window.
- Rollback preflight check: one click roll-back that archives probes + incident metadata.

Post-run artifacts (must do within 24h):
- Custodian fill quick-run notes: what changed, top signals, actions taken, outstanding items.
- Attach example inputs that triggered safety or failures.
- Rate-limit review: if cost/exposure concerns, schedule model tuning or quantization followup.

Open questions / design tensions (working):
- How to balance sample size for A/B power vs user risk for high-sensitivity cohorts?
- Should safety flags always force rollback or only pause for human adjudication? (depends on flag severity taxonomy)
- SRE: what alert latencies are acceptable for canary vs prod SLOs?

Quick checklist (tick-box style - for the custodian):
- [ ] Confirm launch hypothesis and metrics with Steward
- [ ] Validate telemetry & probes exist
- [ ] Run synthetic smoke tests
- [ ] Create canary channel + pin roster
- [ ] Activate at min exposure
- [ ] Monitor windows and snapshot key diffs every step
- [ ] Follow decision heuristics strictly
- [ ] If rollback: run rollback checklist and file incident
- [ ] Post-run: write quick-run notes and share exec summary

Notes to self (snippets):
- Keep templates short — long threads bury the signal.
- Favor deterministic hashing for replays.
- Always capture inputs for safety failures (can't debug without them).

References and links:
- See also: rollout-operator-runbook (internal), safety-flag-taxonomy (Confluence).

TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Add step-by-step console screenshots for pause/rollback (owned: Diego).
- [ ] Implement auto-snapshot generator (owned: Ravi).
- [ ] Draft steward-facing one-pager for A/B power tradeoffs (owned: Maya).
- [ ] Add cost-surge protection guard (SRE owner: Jonah).

End (working doc). This is intentionally compact so a single custodian can run with it. Expect updates after next 2 run rehearsals.
